items.desc: A suspended Miami Gardens police officer whose domestic violence-related charges were dropped is now planning to sue the Opa-locka Police Department, his attorney said Friday.

headlines: CHARGES DROPPED AGAINST SUSPENDED MIAMI GARDENS POLICE OFFICER
NO CHARGES FOR COP SUING OPA-LOCKA POLICE
SUSPENDED MIAMI GARDENS OFFICER CLEARED AND PLANS TO SUE
draft.article:
Suspended Miami Gardens police officer Kolei Kulani McKinney Sr. will not face prosecution following his July arrest by Opa-locka police. The Miami-Dade State Attorney's Office filed a no action decision in the domestic violence case against the 41-year-old officer. McKinney, a 20-year Navy veteran, had been suspended without pay for five months.

His attorney, Stephan Lopez, announced plans to file a lawsuit against the arresting officer and the Opa-locka Police Department, arguing that police lacked probable cause. Lopez is also calling on Miami Gardens to reinstate McKinney with back pay.

The arrest stemmed from alleged July 17 events near Northwest 22nd Avenue and State Road 9.

headlines: NICOLE LOCKLIN SUES MIAMI-DADE ELECTIONS CHIEF FOR VOTE RECORDS
MIAMI-DADE CONGRESSIONAL RACE SPURS LAWSUIT OVER BALLOT RECORDS
WHY DID MIAMI-DADE ELECTION NIGHT TOTALS SUDDENLY SHIFT?
draft.article:
Congressional candidate Nicole Locklin filed a civil lawsuit Thursday against Miami-Dade County Supervisor of Elections Alina García, seeking immediate access to records from the November 3 election.

Locklin ran in Florida’s 26th Congressional District, which spans parts of Miami-Dade and Broward counties. Official tallies place incumbent Mario Díaz-Balart ahead by 1,704 votes, barely avoiding Florida's automatic machine recount threshold.

Locklin points to an election night lead of 2,545 votes that disappeared from tallies without clear explanation. While reports cited a corrected manual data entry error, her lawsuit demands raw vote-counting logs and state transmission records to verify how the county numbers were compiled.

headlines: HUNDREDS OF FLIGHTS CANCELED AT MIA AND FLL SATURDAY
SOUTH FLORIDA AIRPORTS HIT BY MAJOR FLIGHT DELAYS
WHY TRAVELERS AT MIA AND FLL FACE WEEKEND CHAOS
draft.article: South Florida travelers faced major flight disruptions on Saturday across Miami International Airport and Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport. The trouble followed a nationwide Federal Aviation Administration ground stop ordered Friday afternoon due to telecommunications failures in aging air traffic equipment. The Miami-Dade Aviation Department reported 132 cancellations on Saturday at MIA, including 99 arriving flights and 33 departures. Tracking data showed 149 delays at MIA, while FLL logged 142 cancellations and 40 delays during Saturday morning. Friday's ground stop lasted over four hours before being lifted around 8:15 p.m. Federal officials confirmed there was no evidence of a cyberattack, but warned schedules would recover slowly as airlines reposition aircraft.
